_note: What Fallout 4 1.10.163 actually did with this project's scripts on the owner's PC, as reported back (docs/design/VERIFY_LOG.md). tools/papyrus_sim/test_sim.py replays each run in the stand-in engine, with the scripts as they were at that commit, and fails if the stand-in gives a different result. Add a run here only from a real report; never edit a number to make a test pass. From the eleventh run on, a scenario also records the lines the main quest's timing guards wrote to the script log (guard_lines; the report lists them for the whole run, so an empty list is a recorded fact too) and, where a case notes it, whether two handlers overlapped (overlap). A key that begins stand_in_ is not a fact about the game: it tells the replay which of the stand-in's modes to use. Scenario 132 of the eleventh run overlapped in the game, which the stand-in's ordinary mode cannot do at all; it is replayed with every call taking a frame, and the number of tenths waited is then not compared, because that mode provokes overlaps and predicts no timings. A run may carry not_replayed: scenario number, then the key that is not compared, then the reason. It is for lines that came out as they did because of how fast that session of the game happened to run, which the stand-in does not model. The lines themselves are recorded all the same, the replay fails if the stand-in does give them (the exemption is then stale), and everything else about that scenario is compared as usual. From the thirteenth run on a line may also be left out of the replay because it is a place in the game's own test room, which the stand-in does not have; the reason says so.

runs.name: twelfth run, 2026-11-13: all 62 pass with A25 and the lines that say what held the timer back; a slower session

2.guard_lines: Two resolutions overlapped in this session: the caravan master's death was announced while the rescue before it was still being handled, and the guard waited a tenth of a second. Deaths were announced within a fraction of a second in this session, against about a second before. The stand-in's ordinary mode has no time in it, and with calls taking a frame its deaths are still announced later than that.

4.info: Straight after the town stage the caravan master, by then in an alias flagged Essential, was reported as not Essential. In the four runs before she was. The stand-in applies an alias's flags at once.

5.info: The fight did not make the ambush live within eight seconds, though the lead and the player were in combat; it had in the three runs before. The case then set the stage itself, which is its seventh handler. In the stand-in the alias script always hears the fight.

129.guard_lines: Neither the guard nor the fight rule wrote a line: the timer's function found the ambush already resolved, because the death was announced during the calls this version of the case makes between the kill and the timer. In the stand-in those calls take no time.
